title: Data Sciences, B.S. (Eberly College of Science)
notes: Statistical Modeling option, University Park (plan code DTSCS_BS, DTSAB_BS as of this edition -- Penn State Abington added as a second location for this option), built from the real 2024-25 archived bulletin edition (bulletins.psu.edu/archive/2024-2025/undergraduate/colleges/eberly-science/data-sciences-bs/, raw HTML fetched directly; Suggested Academic Plan prints Total Credits 122 for the University Park table, and its own Fall/Spring subtotals -- 15/16, 16/15, 15/16.5, 15/13.5 -- sum to that 122 correctly). This is a genuinely restructured edition, a real drop from the 2023-24 edition's 126 credits down to 122, not a typo: (1) STAT 184 becomes a genuinely real 3-credit course starting with this edition -- confirmed directly against the archived STAT course-description page for this same 2024-25 edition: 'STAT 184: Introduction to R -- 3 Credits' (up from 2 in both the 2022-23 and 2023-24 editions, see those files' notes), and this edition's own UP Suggested Academic Plan table itself also prints 3 in its First Year, Fall cell. This matches stat_catalog.json's current shared 3.0 value and DS-2026.json's own already-verified 3-credit finding for the live 2026-27 edition -- this edition is the real point the credit value actually changed, not a bulletin typo. (The DS program's own 'Common Requirements for the Major (All Options)' summary table, however, still prints a stale '2' for STAT 184 in this and every later edition checked including the live 2026-27 page itself -- that specific summary-table cell simply never got updated; the course-description page and the Suggested Academic Plan table both agree on 3, so 3 is used.) (2) CMPSC 465 (or DS 305) becomes a genuinely new required course starting with this edition -- this edition's own Suggested Academic Plan table adds a footnoted line in Third Year, Spring: 'CMPSC 465 or DS 305' with footnote text 'C or better required and required as a prerequisite for DS 440. For those who enter the major before changes, we will take it as a List B class.' This is a real, dated curriculum change (not present in 2022-23/2023-24, see those files' notes) that is still present, word-for-word identical, on the LIVE 2026-27 bulletin page fetched directly during this same research pass -- meaning DS-2026.json's own notes, which describe removing this exact item after concluding it 'doesn't appear anywhere in the live bulletin,' may need re-checking against a fresh fetch of that page (out of scope to fix here, since this file only covers 2022-2025, but flagging it since it directly contradicts what this edition's -- and the current live edition's -- own page shows). Modeled here as its own required course item, separate from the List B selection pool (the footnote makes clear only PRE-change entrants get to count it toward List B; a student starting under this edition does not). (3) MATH 220 prints at 3 credits in this edition's own Suggested Plan table's First Year, Spring cell (up from 2 in 2022-23/2023-24's own tables) -- but math_catalog.json's shared, university-wide MATH 220 course-description credit range (confirmed via the archived MATH department page for this same edition) is a variable '2-3 Credits,' and the DS program's own Common Requirements summary table for this edition still lists it at a flat 2 (same stale-cell pattern as STAT 184 above, just the opposite direction -- here the summary table is arguably the one that's stale, and the specific printed section credit-hours moved to the 3-credit end of that same real range). Kept at 'credits': 2 here to match math_catalog.json's fixed catalog value (build_full_plan resolves the item's real credit count through the shared catalog regardless of what this field says, same architectural point as STAT 184 above), flagging the printed-3 discrepancy rather than silently picking one. (4) List A / List B Statistical Modeling option course enumeration for this edition is directly confirmed, identical in content to the 2022-23/2023-24 editions: List A (6 credits required) = MATH 435, (MATH 436 or MATH 441), (MATH 451 or MATH 455), MATH 484, (MATH 416/STAT 416), STAT 461, STAT 463, STAT 466, STAT 483; List B (6 credits required, CMPSC 465 still nominally listed here too even though it's now separately required, per the footnote above) = DS 320, DS 330, DS 410, DS 402, IST 461, CMPSC 442, CMPSC 465. Modeled as two 3-credit slots per list (6+6=12), same as prior editions. (5) MATH 21 still has no prerequisite of its own in the current shared math_catalog.json -- same finding and resolution as the 2022-23/2023-24 editions (MATH 21 alone, no MATH 3/4 filler chain); confirmed via build_full_plan (0 'Could not schedule' warnings). GRADUATION TIMELINE: same finding as DS-2022.json/DS-2023.json -- this file's item set fits cleanly in the standard 4 years/8 terms despite the extra CMPSC 465/DS 305 requirement: confirmed via build_full_plan with a same-era start_year=2024/today=2024-07-01 control run at grad_years=4 -- 0 warnings, goal met. Does not itself need the grad_years=5 override Backend/tests.py already carries for DS (see DS-2022.json's notes finding (7) for why the 2026 edition needs it; that override applies uniformly across DS's catalog years and this file still passes cleanly under it too).
